facts.raw_span: An 82-year-old man with epithelioid pleural mesothelioma (cT1N0M0)
was treated with ipilimumab and nivolumab
new bilateral infiltrative shadows
He reported fever and dyspnea
elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels
Krebs von den Lungen-6 was normal
Sputum cultures, procalcitonin, and SARS-CoV-2 PCR were negative

Serologic testing for anti–nuclear antigen, anti–aminoacyl–tRNA synthetase, anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide, anti-Sjögren’s-syndrome-related antigen A and B, and anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antigen antibodies were all negative
no history of antigen exposure
grade 3 ICI-induced pneumonitis was suspected
bronchoscopy showed no airway secretions
Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid contained 29% neutrophils, 58% lymphocytes, 13% macrophages, and a CD4/CD8 ratio of 0.33

was treated with ipilimumab and nivolumab
new bilateral infiltrative shadows
He reported fever and dyspnea
elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels
Krebs von den Lungen-6 was normal
Sputum cultures, procalcitonin, and SARS-CoV-2 PCR were negative

Serologic testing for anti–nuclear antigen, anti–aminoacyl–tRNA synthetase, anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide, anti-Sjögren’s-syndrome-related antigen A and B, and anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antigen antibodies were all negative

concepts.why: The patient developed bilateral infiltrative shadows and symptoms consistent with pneumonitis after receiving ipilimumab and nivolumab, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid analysis showed a high percentage of lymphocytes.
The patient did not respond to methylprednisolone treatment, indicating steroid-refractory disease.
The patient was diagnosed with epithelioid pleural mesothelioma, which is a type of cancer.
The patient developed ICI-induced pneumonitis, which is an immune-related adverse event.
The patient had elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels, indicating an inflammatory response.
The patient had negative serologic testing for various autoimmune antibodies, but the clinical presentation is consistent with an autoimmune disorder.
The patient developed ICI-induced pneumonitis, which is an immunotherapy-related adverse event.
The patient had increasing oxygen requirements and respiratory symptoms, indicating respiratory failure.
The patient developed ICI-induced pneumonitis, which is a complication of cancer treatment.
The patient had elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels, indicating pulmonary inflammation.

It explains the negative sputum cultures, procalcitonin, and SARS-CoV-2 PCR, as well as the negative serologic testing for various antibodies, in the context of the patient's symptoms and treatment with ipilimumab and nivolumab.

rationales.F02: Patient was treated with ipilimumab and nivolumab, which are immunotherapies that can cause ICI-induced pneumonitis.
rationales.F03: New bilateral infiltrative shadows on chest CT suggest pulmonary inflammation.
rationales.F05: Elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels indicate an inflammatory response.
rationales.F07: Negative sputum cultures, procalcitonin, and SARS-CoV-2 PCR rule out other causes of pneumonia.
rationales.F08: Negative serologic testing for various antibodies rules out autoimmune disorders.
rationales.F10: Clinical picture and imaging suggest grade 3 ICI-induced pneumonitis.
rationales.F12: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid analysis shows a high percentage of lymphocytes, consistent with ICI-induced pneumonitis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient was diagnosed with grade 3 ICI-induced pneumonitis and did not respond to steroid treatment, making Steroid-refractory ICI-induced pneumonitis the most specific and accurate diagnosis.
